shared_findings: Phone (all 14 games): the header title is clipped to 'MOTIONAL RELEASE CONSO' and the LVL pill sits on top of it. The mic icon covers the end of the input text ('my boss yelled at me an[mic]e').

Six games (70, 73, 79, 80, 82, 83) use one word-card template: a dark rounded card holding a face sticker of about 22 px inside a dark capsule chip, with the user's word at about 7 px below. The dark chip around the circular face fails the bubble rule. The face changes emotion from word to word but never reacts. In the desktop mid tile of 80 the chip renders empty.

Look-alike gameplay: 73 TRAFFIC LIGHT, 79 MISS ON PURPOSE and 83 SORT STATION are the same game, tap one of 3 or 4 cyan-to-magenta gradient tiles placed above the chip word card. This breaks creative standard 3. 70 and 80 share the same glass-panel layout and 'THOUGHT MOVE ·' pill. 72 and 84 share the same flat glass word pill. 78 and 81 share the same small gradient word chips.

The dark pill toast ('YESSS', 'CLEAN HIT', 'GONE', '+ STILL HIT · CHAIN ×N', with text of about 4 px that can't be read) lands on the control being played in 13 of 14 phone mid or finish tiles: the action pill or tiles in 70, 72, 73, 74, 76, 78, 79, 81, 82 and 83, the card in 84, the drop in 75 and the guide card in 77.

Finales are all shared. The white centre-flash blob appears in 70, 76, 79 and 82. The ray burst plus the tilted 'RELEASED · SHIFT COMPLETE' card appears in 73, 75 and 80. Every game then shows the same 'RELEASE COMPLETE / FEEL A SHIFT?' card, with beige PREVIOUS and NEXT pills floating outside it. In the desktop reveal tiles of 73, 76, 80, 81, 83 and 84 the card is missing, leaving only the two pills in an empty nebula. 70 and 74 never reached a reveal on either size (timeout).
None of the 14 games has an in-world character. The six template games have a static chip sticker. The other eight have nothing beyond the blurred ambient decals at the stage edges.
The HUD contradicts itself. The counter reads '1/6' while the bar shows 100% (70 and 74 finish, 81 finish, 76 mid), and '4/6' at 100% in 79.
Functional: 77 desktop stalls at 67% because the brake drag selects the input text (the desktop end tile shows the input highlighted). Every other game finishes on both sizes, with no errors.

Perf: under headless software rendering every game is above p95 > 34 ms and max > 120 ms (fleet medians: phone p95 433 ms, desktop p95 783 ms). Relative outliers: 72 phone p95 1783 ms with a 1776 ms long task; 82 desktop has a 3811 ms long task; 80 desktop 1649 ms; 70 phone 143 long tasks totalling 30 s (max 1358 ms); 74 desktop p95 1383 ms; 73 phone p95 1067 ms with 1141 to 1253 ms long tasks. Heap growth is at most 7.2 MB (83 desktop).

games.name: METRONOME
games.character_role: A static sticker of about 22 px inside a dark capsule chip, on a dark word card under the pendulum (phone start and mid zoom). Its emotion changes from word to word (purple in phone start, red-orange in desktop finish), but it never moves, squashes or reacts to a tap or a skipped beat. It does not ride, push or fight the metronome. At finish it is washed out under the white flash blob (phone finish).
games.finale: No reveal was captured on either size (metrics reason 'timeout'; the desktop run needed 71 s). The phone finish tile shows the shared white centre-flash blob over the word card and a '+STILL HIT · CHAIN ×6' toast sitting on the THOUGHT MOVE button. The counter reads '1/6' while the bar says 100%. Nothing is metronome-specific: the pendulum does not slow, stop or chime.
games.score_rationale: A3: the 'metronome' is a single pale-cyan line pivoting above a dark glass card. It has no body, wood, brass or weight, no light source and no shadow (phone start). B3: the pendulum line is the only game-specific element, and it sits on the shared nebula and ring stage inside the same glass-panel word-card template as 80, 73, 79, 82 and 83. C3: a pill tap. The mid tile shows no beat pulse or lamp, and per the catalog an off-beat tap gives only a quiet click and no fail signal, so the inhibition moment has no feedback. D2: a static decal in a dark chip. E2: no reveal, only the generic flash blob. F4: 'TAP EVERY SECOND BEAT' is large and clear (phone start), but nothing marks even versus odd beats except the small 'BEAT 16' number, and in phone mid the toast covers the instruction. G4: the button is big, but the header is clipped, the toast covers the button label (phone mid and finish), and the user's word is about 7 px. H5: beat-skipping as impulse practice suits anger, but without a visible temptation or fail it reads as plain tapping.

games.strengths: The concept is a real inhibition exercise. The instruction pill is the largest, clearest text on the screen (phone start), and the pendulum gives a readable rhythm at a glance.
games.problems: Phone start and mid: the face sits in a dark capsule chip, which fails the bubble rule, and the user's word 'my boss' is about 7 px. Phone mid and finish: the toast covers the THOUGHT MOVE button. Phone finish: '1/6' while the bar shows 100%, and the white blob hides the card. No reveal on either size (REVEAL-NONE tiles). There is no metronome body, no beat lamp, no fail feedback and no character participation. The header is clipped and the mic icon covers the input text on phone.
improvements: Build a real metronome: a walnut pyramid body with a brass pendulum and sliding weight, a warm key light from the upper left and a floor shadow. Add a beat lamp that ticks on every beat and glows gold on the even (tap) beats, so 'every second beat' is visible, not counted.

Put an angry character on the pendulum weight. It rides the swing, squashes on each tick and crouches (anticipation) on odd beats, as if to jump. An odd-beat tap makes it bonk with a red wobble and a muted thunk, a visible fail. Each correct skip cools its face from red to orange to calm, and its swing visibly slows.
Implement the catalog's bait taps: odd beats shimmer and pulse brighter to tempt the player, so resisting them feels like a choice.

Finale: the pendulum decelerates and stops, a soft bell chimes, and the character climbs down and sits. The red strobe light of the room fades to amber evening light. Then make sure the reveal fires (it timed out on both sizes).
Move the toast above the stage so it never sits on the tap button. Print the user's word on the metronome face at 15 px or more, and drop the dark chip for a circular face with the text below it.

games.problems: Phone mid and finish: the toast covers the FACT / STORY / MAYBE buttons. Phone finish: the 'panic' card is clipped by the right stage edge. improvements: Give the cards flight in a scene, such as thought-moths fluttering over a dusk meadow on a curved path with wing flaps. The player taps the moth itself (a hit test on the card), and a net sweep with squash and a catch puff confirms it.

Keep the label buttons always visible and at least 44 px tall with 14 px text: move the toast to the top of the stage and never overlay the choice row.
Finale: the three jars line up on a shelf and glow like lanterns, lighting the meadow, while the remaining moths settle as fireflies. The character sits back and smiles.

B4: the 4×3 grid is a recognisable layout of its own, but it floats on the shared nebula.
